newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends higher but crude stays off on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends higher but crude stays off on Iraq.

text.p: IPE gas oil closed stronger on Friday in thin volume having spent most of the day tracking crude.
May IPE gas oil last traded 75 cents higher at $165.50 a tonne having earlier tested, but failed to break, resistance of $167.00, which was to be the contract's intra-day high.
Good support remains at $163.00 with resistance unchanged at $167.00, traders said.
Gas oil spent the early part of the day catching up to crude's late Thursday gains, but started to shed weight once the market started to turn against crude.
"Crude was a touch overdone last night on Iraq and everything which turned out to be untrue, so it's had to correct and that pulled gas oil down as well," said an IPE trader.
The United Nations earlier on Friday said that a report claiming some of its staff in northern Iraq had been arrested by a Kurdish group was untrue.
June Brent was trading at $18.31 a barrel at 1653 GMT, down 10 cents after managing to break through to an intra-day high of $18.55.
"Not much is going on, although we may see some longs come in later, so I wouldn't write Brent off just yet," said one crude IPE trader.
Support was pegged at $18.20 and then $18.18 with resistance at $18.39.
